G-F041.trick: Name a stratified tissue by its TOP layer, like naming a cake by its frosting.
G-F041.tip: For stratified epithelium, only the apical (surface) cell shape counts toward the name.

G-F042.trick: Mucus is the flypaper; cilia are the conveyor belt. No belt = sticky gunk stays put.
G-F042.tip: Separate the jobs: goblet cells make mucus, cilia move it. Lose the cilia and clearance fails.

G-F043.trick: Wet and rubbed (mouth, esophagus, vagina) = many layers, NO dead keratin cap.
G-F043.tip: Keratinized = dry skin surface. Nonkeratinized = moist linings that still face friction.

G-F044.trick: ENDOcrine = released INTO the blood, no duct. EXOcrine = EXITs through a duct.
G-F044.tip: Hormones in the bloodstream = endocrine. Sweat, saliva and digestive enzymes through a duct = exocrine.

G-F045.trick: ELASTIC fibers are rubber bands: stretch and snap back. Collagen is rope: strong, doesn't stretch.
G-F045.tip: Recoil = elastic fibers. Strength against pulling = collagen. Mesh framework = reticular.

G-F046.trick: Dense IRREGULAR = a woven basket: fibers run every way, so it resists pulls from every way.
G-F046.tip: Regular = parallel fibers, one direction (tendons). Irregular = many directions (dermis).

G-F047.trick: RETICular = a neT (reticulum = little net) that holds immune cells in place.
G-F047.tip: Lymph nodes, spleen and bone marrow are framed by reticular tissue.

G-F048.trick: Blood is connective tissue in liquid form: cells floating in a fluid matrix (plasma).
G-F048.tip: Every connective tissue = cells + matrix. In blood, the matrix is plasma.

G-F049.trick: SMOOTH muscle = slow, steady squeezing you can't control, like the gut's toothpaste-tube push.
G-F049.tip: Hollow organ walls + involuntary = smooth muscle. Striated + voluntary = skeletal. Striated + involuntary = cardiac.

G-F050.trick: SERous = SERUM-like slippery fluid between organ and wall so organs glide.
G-F050.tip: Serous membranes line closed ventral cavities. Mucous membranes line tubes that open to the outside.

C-ch5-epithelia.trick: EPI-thelium = ON TOP: it covers and lines every surface.
C-ch5-epithelia.tip: Epithelium has no blood vessels (avascular), sits on a basement membrane, and regenerates quickly.

C-ch5-simple.trick: ENDO-thelium = lining INSIDE vessels: a single, smooth, thin layer.
C-ch5-simple.tip: Thin simple squamous layers are for fast exchange (vessels, alveoli).

C-ch5-stratified.trick: KERATIN comes from the Greek word for horn: the same tough protein makes hair, nails and the outer skin.
C-ch5-stratified.tip: Keratin waterproofs and toughens. Its presence makes stratified squamous "keratinized".

C-ch5-glands.trick: EXOcrine = EXIT through a duct (sweat, saliva).
C-ch5-glands.tip: Duct = exocrine. No duct, into the blood = endocrine.

C-ch5-matrix.trick: Matrix = the Jell-O (ground substance) with fruit strings (fibers) holding the cells.
C-ch5-matrix.tip: Extracellular matrix = ground substance + fibers. It decides how a connective tissue behaves.

C-ch5-connective.trick: CHONDRO = cartilage (like the chondral in costochondral). -cyte = cell.
C-ch5-connective.tip: Chondrocyte = cartilage, osteocyte = bone. Both live in little spaces called lacunae.

C-ch5-membranes.trick: SYNOVIAL = like egg white (syn + ovum): slippery joint fluid made by this lining.
C-ch5-membranes.tip: Synovial membranes are connective tissue only, with no epithelium. They line freely movable joints.
